question: What is the standard timeframe for defining infertility in women under the age of thirty-five?
explanation: Standard clinical guidelines classify infertility in younger women after one full year of regular, unprotected intercourse without conception. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why is the diagnostic threshold for infertility shortened for women aged thirty-five and older?

options.A: Higher prevalence of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Decreased frequency of sexual intercourse over time
options.C: Increased likelihood of male factor contribution with age
options.D: Rapid age-related decline in ovarian reserve and egg quality

explanation: Biological aging significantly accelerates the depletion and chromosomal degradation of oocytes, necessitating earlier clinical evaluation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h1)

question: Which modifiable lifestyle factor directly damages sperm DNA motility and accelerates follicular depletion?
explanation: Tobacco smoke contains toxic metabolites that induce oxidative stress, impairing gamete quality in both sexes. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: How does severe obesity primarily disrupt female reproductive function?

options.A: By accelerating the natural menopause transition by a decade
options.B: By causing direct physical blockage of the fallopian tubes via adipose deposits
options.C: By inducing insulin resistance and altering the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis
options.D: By completely arresting estrogen production in the adrenal cortex

explanation: Adipose tissue alters hormonal feedback loops and peripheral estrogen conversion, frequently resulting in anovulatory cycles. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: Which two pathogens are most frequently implicated in tubal factor infertility due to asymptomatic infections?

options.C: Herpes simplex virus and Human papillomavirus

explanation: These bacterial pathogens are notorious for causing silent upper tract inflammation that leads to irreversible tubal scarring. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is the primary pathological mechanism by which pelvic inflammatory disease causes female infertility?

options.A: Formation of fibrous scar tissue and adhesions blocking the fallopian tubes
options.B: Complete thinning of the endometrial lining preventing implantation
options.C: Direct destruction of all primordial ovarian follicles
options.D: Permanent suppression of luteinizing hormone secretion

explanation: The inflammatory healing response creates adhesions that mechanically obstruct the passage of eggs and sperm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h3)

question: A male factory worker exposed to chronic high ambient heat near industrial furnaces is most at risk for which reproductive issue?

options.A: Complete blockage of the vas deferens from localized burns
options.B: Impaired spermatogenesis due to elevated scrotal temperature
options.C: Premature degradation of the prostate gland epithelium
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of mature testosterone receptors

explanation: Normal sperm production requires a scrotal temperature slightly below core body heat; chronic heat exposure disrupts this process. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h4)

question: Which class of occupational chemical exposures is most commonly linked to endocrine disruption and impaired gametogenesis?
explanation: Substances like lead, mercury, and various industrial solvents cross biological barriers to interfere with hormone production and cellular division. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h4)

question: What is the primary characteristic of endometriosis that contributes to pelvic pain and infertility?

options.A: Overproduction of progesterone leading to premature endometrial shedding
options.B: Hypertrophic enlargement of the cervix blocking cervical mucus production
options.C: Presence of endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity causing inflammation and scarring
options.D: Complete absence of the myometrium within the lower uterine segment

explanation: Ectopic endometrial tissue responds to hormonal cycles by bleeding into enclosed spaces, generating inflammation, adhesions, and pain. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h5)

question: Which clinical manifestation is most characteristic of polycystic ovary syndrome in women of reproductive age?

options.A: Complete cessation of pituitary follicle-stimulating hormone secretion
options.B: Profuse uterine hemorrhage occurring at predictable monthly intervals
options.C: Chronic anovulation accompanied by signs of hyperandrogenism
options.D: Severe cyclic lower abdominal pain with normal menstrual flow

explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome is an endocrine disorder classically marked by irregular or absent ovulation and elevated androgen levels. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is a primary barrier that nurses must overcome when addressing infertility prevention in conservative community settings?

options.A: Cultural stigma and silence surrounding sexual health and reproductive struggles
options.B: A total lack of available pharmacological treatments in modern medicine
options.C: Patients refusing to take routine diagnostic blood tests
options.D: Strict government bans on discussing sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Social stigma often causes individuals to hide symptoms or delay seeking help, making proactive nursing engagement essential. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h6)

question: Which action best exemplifies the nurse's advocacy role in reproductive health prevention?

options.A: Promoting accessible sexual health education and safe workplace environmental policies
options.B: Prescribing specialized hormone replacement therapies independently
options.C: Performing surgical procedures to clear blocked fallopian tubes
options.D: Diagnosing complex endocrine disorders without medical oversight

explanation: Nurses advocate for patients by supporting health literacy, preventive screening programs, and safe environments free of reproductive toxins. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h6)
